summary: Granite-breakwater light at the east side of Gloucester harbour, Massachusetts; a fixed white light from 1905 with an electric fog bell from 1911, now automated.

light.fog_signal: electric fog bell from 1911; electronic horn later (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: wooden tripod, then white house and tower on skeleton substructure
structures.note: Replacement tower and house soon after the 1910 request (LighthouseFriends).

staffing.note: Eastern Point and breakwater lights automated in 1985 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Open from sunup to sundown in good weather; closed to the public when the fog signal sounds (LighthouseFriends).

facts.ownership: Breakwater is within a 53-acre nature preserve owned by Massachusetts Audubon (LighthouseFriends); light managed by the Coast Guard

events.note: Eastern Point Light lit; ships still struck Dog Bar Reef afterwards (LighthouseFriends).
Army Corps of Engineers began the breakwater from Eastern Point, completed by 1905 (LighthouseFriends).
Gloucester Breakwater gas buoy extinguished and relighted 21 August 1900 (Board's report, fiscal 1901).
Fixed red lens lantern on an iron spindle at the breakwater's end, 1 July 1901 (LighthouseFriends).
Storm of 5 November 1901 damaged the spindle and carried away the lens lantern (LighthouseFriends).
Marion, a gasoline launch, stranded on Dog Bar breakwater at 8.40 p.m. on 12 August 1902; the report attributes it to a mistake in locating lights.
Schooner Flo F. Mader struck the unfinished breakwater in a northeast gale on 5 December 1902; crew of six rescued by Dolliver's Neck lifesavers.
Schooner Nautilus dragged onto the breakwater in a heavy NE gale on 13 November 1904 and was lost; crew of four rescued by the station's surfmen.
Wooden tripod with a fixed white light established on the breakwater on 4 December 1905 (LighthouseFriends; USLHS gives ca. 1905).
Relit by the Eastern Point keeper: Breakwater light went out at 2 a.m.; the Eastern Point keeper went out and relit it. Report year to 30 June 1906; exact date not in the extract read.
Electric fog bell placed in operation at the breakwater light on 1 July 1911 (Lighthouse Service Bulletin; LighthouseFriends).
Severe northeasterly gale in early March 1931 washed granite blocks off the breakwater and broke the cable feeding the light and fog bell (LighthouseFriends).
Fire on 17 February 1943 destroyed nearly all of the fog bell house; rebuilt (LighthouseFriends).
Eastern Point Light and Dog Bar Breakwater Light automated; a sensor now activates the electronic fog signal at the breakwater's end (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: George F. Bailey
keepers.note: Keeper of Eastern Point Light, which also tended this light from 1905 (LighthouseFriends). Only the 1902 episode is sourced here; tenure unknown. LighthouseFriends housed the Flo F. Mader's crew with him. The Boston Globe item quoted by the 1903 Life-Saving report names 'Captain George E. Bailey' for the Beta rescue: the middle initial differs and the two are not linked in any source.

keepers.name: Wheeler
keepers.note: Named only as 'Assistant Keeper Wheeler' of Eastern Point Light in the Globe item quoted by the 1903 Life-Saving report; no first name given.

wrecks.outcome: Stranded on Dog Bar breakwater about a mile southeast of the station at 8.40 p.m.; the report attributes it to a mistake in locating lights.

wrecks.vessel: Flo F. Mader (schooner, Lunenburg, Nova Scotia)
wrecks.outcome: Struck the unfinished breakwater in a northeast gale; the crew of six was rescued by Dolliver's Neck lifesavers and landed at Eastern Point; the vessel was floated later, leaking.
Dragged onto the breakwater in a heavy NE gale and lost; the four-man crew was rescued.

notes_for_editor: No keeper roster in the USLHS archive for this light. Keepers named are Eastern Point Light keepers who tended the breakwater light (LighthouseFriends). Name conflict: LighthouseFriends George F. Bailey; the 1903 Life-Saving report, quoting the Boston Globe, George E. Bailey (a different November 1902 rescue). Left unresolved. The 1903 Globe item is second-hand, cited as quoted in the report. The 1901 Board entry is OCR-garbled in its name; only the cleanly OCR'd clause is quoted. The 1905 establishment, 1910 request, 1943 fire, 1985 automation and the Massachusetts Audubon ownership rest on LighthouseFriends only; the Mass Audubon Eastern Point page read did not mention the breakwater. LighthouseFriends quotes the Board's 1910 request; the Board's own 1910 report is not in the corpus. The breakwater's finished length (2,250 ft per LighthouseFriends) was not checked in a primary source. The 1906 relight date is only the year of the report (fiscal 1906). Gas buoy chronology: LighthouseFriends describes a gas buoy placed after the post light proved hard to maintain, with no date; the Board's FY1901 report lists a Gloucester Breakwater item relighted 21 August 1900, before the November 1901 storm that carried the lantern away. The sources do not fix the order, and the story says so. Worcester Spy's length figure is an OCR-damaged number and is not used. The Coast Guard list (current status) was not checked; the record says active. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts only, no quotations beyond evidence fragments. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1901 Board entry name is OCR-damaged ('ga^ ouoy'); the gas-buoy reading rests on that line and the Board's gas-buoy list, not on the page image. Unsourced 'characteristic', 'focal_height_m' and 'range_nm' values were removed from facts. The 1901 entry and LighthouseFriends' date for the gas buoy disagree on order; the story states it. The Worcester Spy says the Mader was floated that afternoon and leaking; LighthouseFriends calls the loss total; both are in the story.
